cohort: 717,080 women who had elective cesarean sections at term
finding: Overweight and obese women who undergo elective cesarean sections before 39 weeks are at greater risk of adverse newborn outcomes, including assisted ventilation, admission to intensive care units, and infant mortality.
mod_finding: Elective cesarean section before 39 weeks was associated with increased risk for adverse outcomes, and this effect was not modified by use of corticosteroids.
